source.title: Gradient Descent for Deep Matrix Factorization: Dynamics and Implicit Bias towards Low Rank
source.authors: Hung-Hsu Chou; Carsten Gieshoff; J. Maly; Holger Rauhut

record.file_problem: The supplied text appears to contain the full paper; no material truncation or garbling is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies implicit low-rank bias in deep linear matrix factorization and denoising. Its results do not test any listed claim version about natural-label test error, the training–test gap, or properties tracking that gap.
record.gate_note: The MNIST denoising experiment reports training error, generalization error and effective rank, but its generalization measure is matrix reconstruction error against the clean matrix, not held-out natural-label test error or the training–test gap described in the claim. The paper also mentions generalization observations from cited work; those are not this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study analyzes spectral dynamics and implicit low-rank bias in deep linear matrix factorization. Its MNIST experiment measures reconstruction of the same clean images from noisy matrices, not held-out classification performance. It does not test any of V1–V8; the relevant classification generalization findings in its introduction are cited results.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors rigorously characterize spectral dynamics and intervals of low effective rank under restricted matrix-factorization assumptions, and present numerical evidence extending these observations, including MNIST denoising. They regard implications for broader deep-learning generalization as prospective.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes deep linear matrix factorization with squared Frobenius reconstruction loss and tests denoising on MNIST, rather than the claim's natural-label classification and held-out accuracy setup.
record.method_sensitivity: Factorization depth changes the reported denoising behavior: N = 2, 3, 4 show low-rank iterates early in optimization, while N = 1 iterates have high rank.

fits_no_version.finding: For noisy matrices containing 100 MNIST images of ones, factorization depths N = 2, 3, 4 produce early low-rank iterates and permit denoising with appropriate stopping; N = 1 does not show the reported denoising behavior.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Deep linear matrix factorization can support denoising through implicit low-rank bias and early stopping.

record.peer_reviewed: Social Science Research Network (as supplied; paper identifies itself as arXiv:2011.13772v5)
record.problems: The generalization error is reconstruction error against the clean matrix, not held-out classification error. The MNIST denoising findings are presented in plots without numerical values in the text. The experiment uses 100 images and does not provide uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for training error or effective rank: they are not held-out natural-label test error or a training–test gap, and the claim versions do not cover them. Figure 9a and 9c report those quantities by depth; their inclusion would not test a listed version.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and the comparison of held-out accuracy under natural versus random labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected classification performance and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under different tuning regimes.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout effects on held-out classification error across training-set sizes and augmentation regimes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, its association with training–test gaps, and comparisons with other generalization measures.
Test-accuracy effects of removing memorized examples versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The states indicate that these measures cannot establish any listed version, not that denoising is undetermined: the text explicitly reports its qualitative presence for factorized models. Varying depth is not the width comparison in V2, and effective rank is not the magnitude-aware sharpness measure in V7.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label held-out accuracy.
Width beyond interpolation and test error across widths.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification generalization.
Large versus small batch generalization under epoch budgets.
Dropout's effect on held-out classification error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the training–test gap.
Effect of removing memorized examples on held-out accuracy.

rows.subject: Deep matrix factorization, N = 1
rows.stage_stated: gradient descent until loss smaller than 10−5 ∥W̃∥F
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent on noisy MNIST matrix reconstruction with factorization depth N = 1.

conditions.value: zero mean Gaussian random matrices, standard deviation σ = 1/√n

rows.measure: Relative approximation error to WLR, shown as generalization error in Figure 9b.
rows.note: Text says the N = 1 version does not allow denoising when stopped at an appropriate time; plotted numerical values are not stated.
rows.check: No listed version is measured. Correct the stopping threshold to loss below 10^-5 times the squared Frobenius norm of the noisy matrix. Figure 9b includes best rank-one and rank-two reconstruction benchmarks, so baseline is not entirely unstated. Numerical curve values are unavailable in the supplied text.
